Standard: The complete primary and backup breathing systems will be in compliance with MIL- STD-3050, Detailed Requirements paragraphs, throughout all phases of flight (e.g., taxi, takeoff, cruise, flight maneuvers, approach, landing), air vehicle altitudes and g loads, as well as during all applicable operational environments (e.g., CBRN). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine the breathing system specifications to ensure all phases of flight are accounted for in the oxygen system hardware.
(2) Review FMECA to verify that all breathing system components are covered.
(3) Examine component hardware configuration documents to confirm compliance with hardware drawings. Analysis.
  (1) Verify that oxygen system safety analysis is included in the SSA and shows that failures across the system are detected, annunciated, and have automatic responses. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct system-level testing of all breathing system components (e.g., AFE, regulator, and air-plumbing) together to determine their functional performance within the breathing system, to include failure mechanisms, to ensure all failure modes are identified and reliability is understood.
    (2) Lab test: Conduct system-level testing to characterize breathing system performance within the intended air vehicle envelope, to include failure modes and mechanisms as well as proper detection and annunciation of alerts. The entire breathing system will be tested as indicated in MIL-STD-3050, Contractor Verification and Validation of ACBS and Government Verification and Validation of ACBS sections. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Flight test: Flight test data confirms conformance with MIL-STD-3050, Detailed Requirements paragraphs.
